boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.headline: BOJ officials signal rate hikes every few months; 30yr JGB yields at 3.88%, 10yr at 2.61% — carry trade unwind risk acute
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.summary: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.25% at the October 29–30 meeting but its September minutes explicitly flagged the case for further hikes, with markets pricing a December move to 1.50%. The 30-year JGB yield stands at 3.83%—73bp above a year ago—driven by a combination of BOJ normalisation, Japan's fiscal expansion programme and the global energy-shock repricing of real rates. Real wages rose for a ninth consecutive month in September, reinforcing the hike narrative.
boj-officials-signal-rate-hikes-every-fe.rationale: The 30-year JGB yield at 3.83% (up 73bp YoY) is a material update to the s2_japan tracker. A December hike to 1.50% would further compress the yen carry-trade spread and tighten the fiscal arithmetic. The Takaichi-plan financing clarity indicator should also be reviewed: Oxford Economics has raised its end-2026 10-year JGB yield forecast to 2.8% and flags ongoing fiscal expansion risk, keeping that rubric at '1 unclear'. The yen carry-trade unwind risk (USD/JPY implications) remains live.

strait-of-hormuz-partial-reopening-in-ea.headline: Strait of Hormuz: partial reopening in early June after ~3-month near-total blockade, but mines uncleared and flows well below pre-war levels (as of late June 2026)
strait-of-hormuz-partial-reopening-in-ea.summary: The 2026 Iran-war Hormuz disruption remains the dominant macro shock in energy markets, with the IEA characterising it as the largest oil-supply disruption in history (~12 Mbpd net shortfall). On November 9, oil fell ~4% as Trump signalled diplomatic restraint on Iran, but a drone strike suspending production at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field and a Houthi missile hitting an Aramco building in Riyadh underscore that physical supply-chain fragility persists.
strait-of-hormuz-partial-reopening-in-ea.rationale: The Hormuz/Red Sea status indicator in s20_sea_lanes should be maintained at '2 closed/contested'. The Nov-9 Khor Mor gas-field drone strike is a fresh incremental supply disruption (Iraq gas, not just Hormuz crude) and the Aramco symbolic strike keeps escalation risk alive even as Trump's diplomatic signalling temporarily depressed prices. WTI/Brent price and the Hormuz status indicator both require updates. The energy shock also feeds directly into s18_food_fertilizer (Qatar LNG force-majeure affects nitrogen-fertilizer feedstock) and s4_dev_debt (EM energy-import bills surging).

china-japan-rare-earth-dual-use-controls.headline: China–Japan Rare-Earth / Dual-Use Controls Expand to Trigger GDP-Level Supply Chain Risk; November 2026 Broader Suspension Expiry Looms
china-japan-rare-earth-dual-use-controls.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce on Nov 9 formally extended the suspension of October-2025 rare-earth export controls—covering 7 heavy rare earths, superhard materials, magnet/recycling technology, and the extraterritorial 0.1% rule—for two additional months, alongside a parallel pause on a 24% tariff surcharge on US goods. The extension preserves the Busan/Oct-2025 trade truce ahead of an expected Trump-Xi APEC summit in Shenzhen, but leaves the April-2025 licensing regime for dysprosium, terbium, and five other heavy rare earths intact.
china-japan-rare-earth-dual-use-controls.rationale: The Nov-10 pause-expiry date was the single most watched trigger in s6_rare_earths. The 2-month roll (not a full settlement) updates the 'Nov-2025 pause status' indicator from '1 expiring' back to '0 extended', but the April-2025 licensing regime remains live and the Jan-10 cliff now becomes the next critical date. The US defense ban on Chinese-origin rare earths also takes effect Jan 1, 2027, meaning two countdowns now converge inside 60 days. Materially updates the rubric for the pause-status indicator.

synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.headline: Synchronized global sovereign bond rout: US 10y at 4.80%, UK 30y at 5.82% (highest since 1998), German 10y at 2011 highs
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.summary: France's 10-year OAT–Bund spread reached 176 bps on October 23 and stood at 148 bps on November 5—the widest since the 2011 eurozone sovereign-debt crisis—driven by a fiscal deficit estimated at 5.4% of GDP, political paralysis over the budget, and a November 3 budget revenue-vote that failed to restore confidence. A Moody's rating review is due November 27, and analysts warn that a downgrade or continued spread widening toward 200 bps could trigger contagion to Italy and test ECB TPI activation eligibility.
synchronized-global-sovereign-bond-rout-.rationale: The OAT-Bund spread has escalated materially since the last tracker update—now at multi-year highs and approaching a critical Moody's review date (Nov 27). The Rating action indicator for s10_france should be upgraded from '1 negative outlook' toward '2 downgrade' watch. The budget vote failure and ECB's explicit reluctance to invoke TPI for France (due to deficit disqualification) make this a live systemic risk for eurozone fragility, not just a French idiosyncratic story.

nasdaq-enters-correction-11-9-after-demo.headline: Nasdaq enters correction (-11.9%) after Democratic midterm sweep triggers data-center moratorium fears
nasdaq-enters-correction-11-9-after-demo.summary: On November 5, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% and the Nasdaq-100 dropped 6.4%—its worst single day since March 2020—wiping ~$2.5 trillion in market value as investors priced in tighter AI-infrastructure regulation following Democratic 'blue-wave' midterm victories. 40 of 41 state ballot measures on data-center construction restrictions passed, and ING simultaneously sought to offload a $500M portfolio of 12 data-center loans, the first visible bank-to-private-credit deleveraging in AI infrastructure.

proposed_indicator.label: AI-capex political/regulatory headwind (0 none / 1 emerging / 2 acute)
proposed_indicator.rubric: 0 = no material legislative or ballot-measure threat to data-center construction pipeline; 1 = isolated state-level moratoria or proposed regulation affecting <10% of planned US capacity; 2 = multi-state moratoria or federal legislation that credibly delays >10% of the announced hyperscaler/Stargate capex pipeline. Current reading: 2 (40/41 ballot measures passed restricting data-center construction across 10 states; Texas Governor-elect campaigned on a moratorium).

nasdaq-enters-correction-11-9-after-demo.rationale: s8_ai_capex already tracks capex-vs-revenue gap and GPU-backed debt stress, but has no indicator for the political/regulatory risk to the construction pipeline itself. The midterm ballot-measure wave is a structurally new transmission channel: it simultaneously raises the capex overhang risk (projects delayed = sunk-cost debt with no revenue) and the GPU-backed debt refinancing stress. The ING loan-sale is a leading edge of GPU/data-center debt redistribution into private credit (crosslinks s3_private_credit). A new ordinal indicator is needed to track this dimension.

euro-area-ppi-hits-record-11-1-global-en.headline: Euro Area PPI hits record 11.1%; global energy shock feeding sticky upstream inflation and ECB rate-hike pressure
euro-area-ppi-hits-record-11-1-global-en.summary: Eurozone producer-price inflation rose to a record 11.1% in October (the highest in the series), driven by energy-cost pass-through from the Hormuz oil shock, with the ECB holding its deposit rate at 2.5% despite inflation hitting a three-year high of 3.8% in September. Markets are pricing a December ECB hike, while China's factory-gate prices rose 5.0% YoY and UK motor-fuel prices were up ~30%, signalling a broad-based, energy-driven PPI shock across major economies.

proposed_story.name: Energy-shock second-round inflation (stagflation corridor)
proposed_story.why: The 2026 Hormuz disruption has now produced a simultaneous, multi-economy PPI surge (Eurozone record 11.1%, China +5.0%, UK fuel +30%) that is feeding into consumer prices and forcing central banks in both developed markets (ECB, BOE, RBA) and emerging markets to tighten even as growth slows. This is distinct from s20_sea_lanes (physical disruption) and s18_food_fertilizer (food/fertilizer specific); it represents a macro-financial transmission risk—rising real rates, compressed corporate margins, EM hard-currency stress from imported inflation—that cuts across multiple existing stories but is not fully captured by any single one. The IMF projects global headline inflation at 4.7% in 2026, and the feedback loop between energy prices, wage expectations, and central-bank credibility is the dominant macro risk for H1 2027.

indicators.label: Eurozone PPI YoY (%)
indicators.rubric: Current: 11.1% (Oct 2026 record). Threshold: >8% = elevated; >10% = acute second-round risk. Source: Eurostat flash PPI release.

indicators.label: Number of G20 CBs actively hiking (count, rolling 3-month)
indicators.rubric: 0–2 = contained; 3–5 = coordinated tightening; 6+ = synchronised shock risk. Tracks ECB, BOE, RBA, Banxico, SARB, etc. Current: at least 4 (ECB Dec hike priced, RBA hiked to 6.85%, EM CBs turning hawkish per Nov-8 data).

indicators.label: Stagflation signal composite (0 no / 1 partial / 2 confirmed)
indicators.rubric: 0 = inflation falling AND growth above trend in all G7; 1 = inflation sticky + growth slowing in ≥2 G7; 2 = inflation rising + contraction in ≥1 G7 or global PMI <49. Current: 1 (inflation sticky across G7, Eurozone growth mixed, UK/Germany stagnating).

euro-area-ppi-hits-record-11-1-global-en.rationale: No existing story fully captures the second-order macro-financial transmission of the Hormuz energy shock into a synchronised global tightening cycle. s20_sea_lanes tracks the physical chokepoint; s18_food_fertilizer tracks food/fertilizer; s4_dev_debt tracks EM debt stress. But the cross-cutting risk—record Eurozone PPI forcing ECB hikes even as growth slows, compressing sovereign fiscal space (France, Italy), raising EM hard-currency debt servicing costs, and tightening the AI-capex financing environment simultaneously—warrants a dedicated story. The IMF's 4.7% global inflation forecast for 2026 and the ECB's reluctance to backstop French debt while also hiking rates is the core fragility.

strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.headline: Strait of Hormuz Effectively Closed by US-Iran War; Brent Above $110–$117, Global Inventories Down ~1 Billion Barrels
strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.summary: The US-Iran war that began February 28, 2026 has cut Hormuz throughput from 21.6 mb/d to ~10.9 mb/d by September, with OPEC+ freezing December targets for a third consecutive month on November 1 and Brent settling at $117.64 on October 30. Peace-talk optimism briefly pushed oil below $100 on November 2, but supply buffers are near exhaustion per ADNOC's CEO.
strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.target_indicator: Hormuz/Red Sea status → update to '2 closed'; WTI crude → ~$100/bbl; Undersea cable incidents → '0 none'
strait-of-hormuz-effectively-closed-by-u.rationale: The Strait of Hormuz is effectively shut (status = 2), representing the single largest physical supply disruption in oil-market history per CEPR/EIA/IEA data. Brent at $117.64 and WTI near $100 are directly captured by the s20 WTI indicator. The diesel/LNG transmission into industrial supply chains and the ~1bn-barrel inventory drawdown (ADNOC CEO, Nov 2) make this the highest-materiality live event in the tracker. The November 2 US-Iran peace-talk signal is a meaningful but fragile downside tail that should be monitored as a potential status shift from '2 closed' toward '1 contested'.

france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.headline: France OAT-Bund Spread Hits 176 bp — Crisis-Era Highs — as Moody's Cuts Outlook to Negative and Budget Vote Looms November 3
france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.summary: The 10-year OAT-Bund spread peaked at 176 bp on October 23 (widest since 2011), settling at 159 bp on October 30 as France's debt-to-GDP reaches 121.7% and a €43bn austerity package faces a divided parliament vote on November 3. Moody's left France at Aa3 but assigned a negative outlook on October 23; S&P review follows November 27.
france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.target_indicator: OAT-Bund 10y spread → 159 bp (peak 176 bp); Govt stability → '1 fragile'; Rating action → '1 negative outlook' (Moody's Aa3/negative, Oct 23)
france-oat-bund-spread-hits-176-bp-crisi.rationale: All three s10 indicators require simultaneous update. The spread has surpassed Italy's and Greece's (now wider-than-PIIGS), debt/GDP at 121.7% is a record, the Moody's negative outlook is a direct rating-action trigger (level 1), and the November 3 budget vote introduces binary tail risk toward level 2 (collapse/snap-election). The S&P review on November 27 is the next scheduled catalyst.

china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.headline: China Rare-Earth Pause Legally Expires November 10; US Commerce Dept Has Not Published Matching Extension Notice
china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.summary: China's suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export-control announcements (Nos. 55–62 including the 0.1%-rule Notice 61) expires under published legal text on November 10, 2026, despite MOFCOM's informal September 28 statement referencing a wider arrangement through January 10, 2027. The US has not issued a formal matching notice, creating a legal ambiguity that could allow controls to snap back in 8 days.
china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.target_indicator: Nov-2025 pause status → update to '1 expiring' (legal text ends Nov 10; informal extension to Jan 10 not yet codified in published Chinese notice); Rare-earth export license flow → '1 slowing' (April 2025 licensing already active; exports fell 9.6% YTD Jan–Sep 2026)
china-rare-earth-pause-legally-expires-n.rationale: The gap between the published suspension-end date (Nov 10) and the informal bilateral extension (Jan 10) is uncodified on the Chinese side and unmatched by a US Federal Register notice—creating an 8-day window where controls could legally re-activate without a further formal announcement. This is precisely the s6 'pause status' indicator scenario at level 1 (expiring). April 2025 heavy-RE licensing (dysprosium, terbium) remains fully in force regardless, keeping license-flow at '1 slowing'.

ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.headline: AI Capex-Debt Collision Drives 30-Year Treasury to 24-Year High (5.67%, Oct 7); CCC Junk Spreads Widen 319 bp Since August
ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.summary: Hyperscalers (Alphabet with negative free cash flow of -$9.1bn in Q3, Meta raising capex floor to $135–145bn) are issuing 20–40-year corporate bonds en masse, competing directly with record sovereign supply and pushing the 30-year Treasury to 5.67% on October 7 (highest since 2002) and widening CCC-rated spreads by 319 bp since late August. The 10-year ACM term premium has surged to +92 bp.
ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.target_indicator: AI capex-vs-revenue gap concern → '2 widening fast' (Alphabet FCF negative; CCC spreads +319bp); GPU-backed debt refinancing stress → '1 signs' (CoreWeave CDS cited as early-warning; broad HY not yet confirmed); US IG OAS → elevated but not yet crisis
ai-capex-debt-collision-drives-30-year-t.rationale: The Alphabet Q3 print (negative FCF, $98.2bn total corporate debt) and Meta's capex raise represent a qualitative regime shift: hyperscalers have flipped from net cash providers to net capital consumers. The AI-debt-Treasury-yield interaction loop (more AI issuance → higher term premium → tighter financial conditions → higher AI borrowing costs) is now cited by the Fed's own market desk and LPL Research. CCC spread widening of 319 bp is a material stress signal for s8, pushing the capex-gap indicator to level 2.
